title: Component Engineer
description:
Job Role: Component Engineer

Job Location: Bangalore

Notic Period: Immediate to 30 days


Who we are:

At UST, we help the world’s best organizations grow and succeed through transformation. Bringing together the right talent, tools, and ideas, we work with our client to co-create lasting change. Together, with over 30,000 employees in 30+ countries, we build for boundless impact—touching billions of lives in the process. Visit us at UST.com.


Summary:

We are seeking a motivated Component Engineering & Alternate Sourcing Analyst to support semiconductor equipment manufacturing and supply chain resiliency. The analyst will evaluate OEM and Build-to-Print (BTP) electrical and electronic components, identify sourcing risks, and drive alternate sourcing, cost reduction, and supply continuity initiatives.


The role requires strong technical knowledge of electrical and electronic components, including controllers, contactors, circuit breakers, relays, connectors, crimps and terminals, DC power supplies, AC-DC converters, sensors, and active and passive board components. The analyst will identify suitable alternates, perform Form-Fit-Function (FFF) comparisons, and evaluate supplier capability, technical specifications, manufacturing processes, cost, and supply risk.


The Opportunity:

Supply Chain Risk Management

  • Analyse single-source risks and assess supplier concentration exposure
  • Review Risk Hub ratings and monitor part shortages and obsolescence
  • Recommend mitigation plans for high-risk components
  • Support Single Point of Failure (SPOF) reduction initiatives


BTP Component Evaluation

  • Review BOM structures and component usage
  • Understand manufacturing and special process requirements
  • Define and evaluate test requirements for component qualification
  • Assess custom-fabricated and engineered components
  • Support supplier transition and source qualification projects


Alternate Sourcing

  • Identify and evaluate alternate sources for SPOF electrical and electronic components
  • Perform Form-Fit-Function (FFF) comparisons between OEM and alternate parts
  • Evaluate supplier capability, technical specifications, manufacturing processes, cost, and supply risk


Data Analytics & Reporting

  • Develop part screening reports and sourcing recommendations
  • Create risk mitigation summaries and dashboards
  • Support management reviews with data-driven recommendations
  • Track sourcing opportunities and qualification status


Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Commodity Managers, Supplier Quality Engineers, Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, and Supply Chain Planning teams


What you need:

Required Skills:

  • Electrical and electronic component knowledge: Working knowledge of controllers, contactors, circuit breakers, relays, connectors, DC power supplies, AC-DC converters, sensors, and active and passive board components.
  • Form-Fit-Function (FFF) evaluation: Ability to compare OEM and alternate parts across electrical, mechanical, and performance specifications and datasheets.
  • Supply chain risk analysis: Understanding of single-source risk, supplier concentration, obsolescence, and part shortages, with the ability to recommend mitigation plans.
  • Alternate source identification: Experience finding and evaluating alternate suppliers for electrical and electronic components, including supplier capability and supply risk.
  • Data analysis and reporting: Proficiency in Microsoft Excel for part screening, risk summaries, and data-driven sourcing recommendations.


Desired Skills:

  • Semiconductor or capital equipment experience: Background in semiconductor equipment manufacturing or other capital equipment industries.
  • Build-to-Print (BTP) supplier experience: Experience working with BTP suppliers and custom or engineered components.
  • Supplier transition and qualification: Experience running supplier transition or source qualification projects, including test and qualification requirements.
  • Risk management platforms: Familiarity with Risk Hub or similar supplier risk management tools.
  • Dashboard and visualization tools: Exposure to Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools for risk and sourcing reporting.


Qualification:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Relevant experience: Experience in component engineering, sourcing, supplier quality, or electronics engineering (years to be set by the hiring manager).
  • Component qualification: Demonstrated experience qualifying components or evaluating alternate parts.
  • Analytical and problem-solving ability: Strong capacity to analyze technical and supply data and reach sound conclusions.
  • Cross-functional collaboration: Proven ability to work with Commodity Management, Supplier Quality, Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, and Supply Chain Planning teams.


What we believe:

We’re proud to embrace the same values that have shaped UST since the beginning. Since day one, we’ve been building enduring relationships and a culture of integrity. And today, it's those same values that are inspiring us to encourage innovation from everyone, to champion diversity and inclusion and to place people at the centre of everything we do.


Humility:

We will listen, learn, be empathetic and help selflessly in our interactions with everyone.


Humanity:

Through business, we will better the lives of those less fortunate than ourselves.


Integrity:

We honour our commitments and act with responsibility in all our relationships.

UST is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We believe that no one should be discriminated against because of their differences, such as age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity and expression, religion, or sexual orientation.


All employment decisions shall be made without regard to age, race, creed, colour, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status or any other basis as protected by federal, state, or local law.

title: Purchasing and Material Planner
location: Mount Druitt, New South Wales, Australia
description:
Job Description

About the role

Like working out why something happened, not just reporting that it did? This could be your next move.

Ever wondered what it takes to keep thousands of much-loved garden products moving off the line and into Aussie and Kiwi backyards? As our Purchasing & Material Planner at Mt Druitt, one of the largest and most complex manufacturing sites in the Yates Group, you'll use data and sharp thinking to make sure production never misses a beat.

You don't need a supply chain background for this role. If you're an analyst in finance, commercial, business or data, and you'd like to see your numbers drive real-world outcomes, we'll teach you the supply chain side. What matters most is your analytical mind, your curiosity and your instinct to ask "is there a better way?"

Working hand in hand with our Production Planner, you'll turn the production plan into action. You'll dig into the data to spot missing components before they become problems, raise purchase orders at the right time and keep raw materials, packaging and third-party bulk flowing to the site.

This role isn't just about keeping things ticking over. We want you to question how we do things, find patterns others miss and help shape a smarter, more efficient supply chain.

You also won't sit behind a screen all day. You'll work with people right across the site, building strong relationships, solving problems together and turning your insights into action.

Our Benefits:

  • Up to $1,000 net annually to cover private health extras gap costs
  • Exclusive discounts on DuluxGroup products and partner offers
  • Stay active anytime, anywhere through our partnership with Fitness Passport
  • 20 weeks paid parental leave (primary carers) and 2 weeks partner leave from day one
  • Market leading learning, development and career pathways
  • Access to our Wellbeing Hub and full EAP support
  • Recognition programs that celebrate your impact

What You'll Bring

  • A strong analytical background, for example as a financial, business, commercial or data analyst
  • Curiosity and critical thinking. You like to understand the "why" and aren't afraid to challenge the status quo
  • Attention to detail and the ability to juggle competing priorities
  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach, with confidence to build relationships at all levels

About Us:

At Yates, we don’t just grow gardens - we grow people, ideas, and communities. We have over 130 years of heritage and the #1 gardening brand in Australia and New Zealand, trusted by generations of growers. The Yates Group also includes Seasol, Munns, and Hortico, all trusted names in garden care.

But we’re more than just Yates. As part of the DuluxGroup, we are connected to a family of iconic, market-leading brands that protect, maintain and enhance the spaces and places in which we live and work.

Our real secret? Our people. We’re proud of the awesome culture we’ve built that is authentic, collaborative, inclusive, and full of energy. So, if you're driven by purpose and want to make a meaningful impact, this is where you belong.

Why Join Us?

Progressing your career with the DuluxGroup means being part of a network of over 8000 employees globally who believe in our purpose to ‘Imagine a Better Place’

With origins dating back to 1918, we are a leading marketer and manufacturer of iconic brands such as Dulux, Selleys, Cabots, Yates and B&D to name a few.

By joining us, you will be a part of a long term strategy to deliver profitable growth through brand leadership, innovation and customer intimacy. We are committed to internal mobility and growth while fostering an inclusive culture with flexible work options.

If this sounds like an environment you would like to be a part of, please apply online!

title: Civil 3D Engineer
description:

title: Data Analyst (Operations)
description:
Data Analyst - Retail Operations & Commercial Insight

£35,000-£37,000
 Leicestershire - Office Based (5 Days Per Week)

I'm hiring a Data Analyst to join the Finance Operations team of one of the UK's largest businesses, supporting a portfolio of major brands operating on a market-leading eCommerce and fulfilment platform.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an analytical problem-solver who enjoys investigating operational issues, working with large datasets, and helping stakeholders make better decisions through data.

The role

You'll sit within the team responsible for supporting partner brands operating on a large-scale platform.

These brands rely on the business for:

  • eCommerce technology
  • Warehousing
  • Logistics
  • Stock management
  • Financial operations

Your role will focus on helping operational teams understand performance, identify issues, and improve outcomes through data.

This isn't a project-heavy role with months-long delivery cycles.

Instead, you'll spend your time solving operational problems, responding to business questions, investigating anomalies, and helping stakeholders understand what is happening within the data.

What you'll be doing



Operational Analytics & Investigation

  • Analyse stock, sales, returns, profitability, and operational performance data.
  • Investigate stock discrepancies and inventory issues.
  • Understand why stores or partners are underperforming.
  • Conduct root-cause analysis on operational incidents and variances.
  • Support stocktake and inventory investigations.

Reporting & Insight

  • Produce KPI and operational reporting across partner brands.
  • Monitor performance against key targets and highlight risks or opportunities.
  • Deliver insight to operational, commercial, and finance stakeholders

Data & Systems

  • Use SQL and Databricks to access and analyse operational datasets.
  • Support migration of reporting into Power BI solutions.
  • Help improve reporting accuracy and data quality.

Stakeholder Management

  • Work closely with operational teams and partner brands.
  • Manage competing requests and priorities.
  • Translate analytical findings into clear recommendations.
  • Build trusted relationships with stakeholders across the business.

What they're looking for



Essential

  • Around 2+ years' experience in an analytical role.
  • Strong SQL skills.
  • Experience with Power BI or a similar visualisation tool.
  • Strong investigative and analytical mindset.
  • Ability to explain findings clearly and confidently.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced operational environment.

Nice to have

  • Databricks exposure.
  • Retail, warehousing, logistics, stock, or supply-chain analytics experience.
  • Experience working with operational performance data.

What matters most

The hiring manager is much more interested in:

  • Root-cause analysis
  • Investigative thinking
  • Stakeholder management
  • Operational insight

than pure dashboard development.

Power BI is useful, but the real value comes from being able to look at a problem, understand what's happening in the data, and explain it clearly.

Why join?

  • Join one of the UK's largest businesses.
  • Work with major brands operating on a leading platform.
  • Huge scope for progression across a large organisation.
  • Varied workload with lots of exposure to different parts of the business.
  • Highly collaborative team environment.
  • Opportunity to develop both technical and commercial skills.

Package

  • £35,000-£37,000 salary
  • Access to one of the UK's largest organisations
  • Significant progression opportunities across the wider business
  • Exposure to modern analytics tools including SQL, Databricks, and Power BI

Working Pattern

Leicestershire

  • 5 days per week onsite
  • Potential future flexibility may exist, but candidates should join expecting full-time office attendance

Interview Process

Stage 1: 30-minute introductory interview

Stage 2: In-person SQL-based analytical assessment and stakeholder discussion

This role would suit a:

  • Data Analyst
  • Operations Analyst
  • Commercial Analyst
  • Retail Analyst
  • Supply Chain Analyst
  • Inventory Analyst

who enjoys solving operational problems, investigating performance issues, and using data to support business decisions.

description:
Description

Who We Are


At JD.com, also known as JINGDONG, everything begins with a bold idea and the drive to make life smarter, faster, and more connected. With competitive compensation, great office locations, and a people-first culture that champions continuous learning, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and kick-start your career.


About Our Program


You’ll be joining the JD Vanguard (JDV) Graduate Program, our frontline leadership pathway for the next generation of supply chain talent. Over the course of a year, you’ll take on real projects, build technical and people-leadership skills, and learn how JD Logistics operates at a global level, with the opportunity to extend and continue your journey.

JD Vanguard Program is a strategic talent supply chain project of JD.com, aiming to build a team of young talent embodying the JD spirit and deeply rooted in frontline operations. With the phased goal of cultivating grassroots managers, it ultimately nurtures mid-level managers who understand frontline operations and can drive strategic implementation.

Job Responsibilities

1, Monitor and inspect incoming goods, verifying compliance with quality standards, specifications, and documentation (e.g., invoices, purchase orders) to ensure accuracy in quantity, condition, and labeling.

2, Conduct regular audits of warehouse storage areas, checking for proper handling, storage conditions (e.g., temperature, humidity), and adherence to safety and hygiene protocols.

3, Inspect outgoing shipments to confirm product integrity, correct packaging, and accurate labeling, minimizing the risk of defects or errors during delivery.

4, Develop and implement quality control checklists and procedures to standardize inspection processes across receiving, storage, and shipping operations.

5, Track and analyze quality-related data (e.g., defect rates, non-conformities, customer complaints) to identify trends, root causes, and areas for improvement.

6, Collaborate with warehouse teams, suppliers, and logistics partners to resolve quality issues, implement corrective actions, and prevent recurrence.

7, Maintain detailed records of inspections, test results, and corrective measures, ensuring compliance with internal policies and regulatory requirements.

8,Train warehouse staff on quality control procedures, emphasizing the importance of accuracy and adherence to standards in daily operations.


Job Requirements

1,Bachelor’s degree in logistics, supply chain management, quality management, or a related field;

2, Strong understanding of quality management systems (e.g., ISO standards) and warehouse safety regulations.

3, Excellent attention to detail and ability to identify defects, discrepancies, or non-conformities in products and processes.

4, Strong analytical skills to interpret quality data, identify trends, and recommend corrective actions.

5, Effective communication and teamwork abilities, with the capacity to collaborate with warehouse teams, suppliers, and cross-functional departments.

6, Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, prioritize tasks, and adapt to changing operational needs.

7, Chinese language skills are a plus.

title: 0485 - Frozen Lead
description:
Position Purpose: Exemplifies and ensures strong customer service in all aspects of the job. Directs and controls the operation of the Frozen Department to achieve sales and profit objectives.

Job Description: As a primary contact for customers, the Frozen Food Manager provides friendly, courteous, and helpful service. Trains, supervises, schedules, and assigns duties to Frozen Food Clerks. Changes signs and prices as directed by merchandising. Responsible for maintaining appropriate stock and inventory in the frozen food area. Responsible for minimizing out of stock product. Writes frozen food order in the order guide book. Checks order for completeness upon arrival. Rotates product and removes expired stock daily. Keeps frozen food cases stocked with product, cleans department area, restocks items in freezer for other departments. Boards received from trucks are loaded onto pallets. Pallets are taken to the sales floor with a pallet jack and product is loaded into cases. Cardboard boxes are broken down and placed in the bailer. Ice machine is checked daily and filled as needed. End displays are restocked as per instructions. Cleans any spills from leakage in cases or on department floor. In event of a freezer malfunction or power outage the employee will remove all items, clean out the case, and replace or restock product. May also function as cashier/checker during peak times.

title: SAP Analyst - SD
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

Reporting to the Manager, Enterprise Applications & Data, the SAP Analyst - SD is an internal IT resource responsible for supporting, stabilizing, and improving SAP S/4HANA business processes within assigned functional areas. The role provides functional support across Sales and Distribution (SD), Logistics Execution (LE), and related integration points as assigned. The incumbent works closely with business process owners, department SMEs, IT technical resources, vendors, and external support partners to resolve issues, support testing and change activities, maintain functional documentation, and help ensure SAP processes operate reliably after go-live.


POSITION RESPONSIBILITES:

Operational Support

  • Maintains a high level of operational support for internal and external customers through:
  • SAP SD/LE incident and request support
  • Problem investigation, root cause analysis, and resolution of recurring issues
  • Functional investigation of reported or monitored Order-to-Cash system exceptions, including blocked orders, incomplete documents, delivery backlogs, unbilled deliveries, and failed EDI/IDoc transactions, in partnership with business process owners
  • Change and release support
  • Testing and validation support
  • Functional documentation and knowledge transfer


SAP Functional Support and Stabilization

  • Supports SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash operation and post-go-live stabilization through:
  • Day-to-day functional support for SD/LE business processes and transactions
  • Independent investigation and resolution of SAP SD/LE functional, configuration, and integration issues, engaging external support partners when specialized expertise or additional resources are required
  • Analysis and resolution of functional issues, data inconsistencies, and process exceptions across sales, delivery, and billing documents
  • Support for order cut-offs, shipping deadlines, billing runs, period-end billing, and other time-sensitive business cycles
  • Identification and reduction of manual workarounds introduced during or after go-live
  • Coordination with business SMEs, IT technical teams, SAP Basis/Security resources, and vendors
  • Escalation of issues requiring specialized technical, integration, or master data expertise after appropriate internal functional investigation



Assigned Module Support and Integration

  • Provides functional support for SAP Sales and Distribution and Logistics Execution, including:
  • Sales order management, including sales document types, item categories, incompletion logs, delivery and billing blocks, and order changes
  • Pricing, including condition records, pricing procedures, discounts, surcharges, freight, and tax determination touchpoints
  • Availability check (ATP/aATP), order confirmation, backorder processing, and product allocation where used
  • Outbound delivery management, delivery configuration, shipping documents, and goods issue integration, coordinating with EWM colleagues responsible for warehouse picking, packing, staging, and loading execution
  • Billing, credit/debit memos, returns, cancellations, rebates or settlement management, and customer credit management blocks
  • Output management for order confirmations, delivery notes, packing lists, bills of lading, and invoices
  • Integration between SD and FI (revenue account determination, accounts receivable), MM, EWM, and PP
  • Troubleshoot and resolve SAP SD-related EDI/IDoc errors involving customer orders, advance ship notices, and invoices, coordinating with the EDI specialist for mapping, connectivity, and partner-related issues.
  • Business Partner (customer) master data, sales area data, customer-material information, and pricing master data


Configuration, Testing, Documentation, and Enhancements

  • Supports controlled SAP changes and continuous improvement through:
  • Hands-on SD/LE functional configuration, troubleshooting, and controlled enhancements, including copy control, output determination, pricing, and account determination, in line with clean core principles
  • Requirement gathering and functional specification development for reports, interfaces, conversions, enhancements, forms, and workflows
  • Participation in system integration testing, user acceptance testing, regression testing, and production validation of end-to-end Order-to-Cash scenarios
  • Support for Fiori apps, document flow, reporting tools, IDoc monitoring, technical logs, and basic troubleshooting activities used to diagnose functional issues
  • Development and maintenance of configuration guides, business process procedures, training materials, and support documentation


Customer Service and Business Partnership

  • Provides effective customer service and business partnership through:
  • Timely response to SAP-related support requests and incident tickets
  • Clear communication with Customer Service, Sales, Warehouse, Logistics, Finance, management, IT, vendors, and support partners
  • Translation of business issues into clear functional requirements or support actions
  • Follow-up with users to confirm acceptance of solutions and resolution of incidents
  • Support for user training, process adoption, and continuous improvement within the Order-to-Cash process
  • Supports the SAP COE operating model by working with business Stream Owners, Department SMEs, and Super Users to validate requirements, support testing, confirm readiness, improve training, and reduce avoidable first-line support escalations to IT.


Data Quality, Controls, and Knowledge Transfer

  • Protects the integrity of the Order-to-Cash process through:
  • Partnering with master data owners to resolve customer, material, and pricing data defects that impact orders, deliveries, and billing
  • Tracking agreed Order-to-Cash measures such as blocked and incomplete orders, delivery backlog, unbilled deliveries, billing errors, and repeat incidents
  • Adherence to change management, audit, and segregation-of-duties requirements for SD/LE changes and production access
  • Structured knowledge transfer from implementation and support partners to build sustainable internal SD capability


SKILLS/EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:


  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Minimum 4 to 6 years of hands-on SAP SD functional experience, preferably including SAP S/4HANA implementation, post-go-live support, or manufacturing experience.
  • Hands-on SAP SD functional experience, including Order-to-Cash processes and SD configuration, is required. Experience with SAP LE, EWM, FI, MM, or related SD integration areas is an asset. Experience troubleshooting SAP SD-related EDI/IDoc errors and understanding their impact on sales orders, outbound deliveries, and billing is an asset.
  • Strong functional knowledge of Order-to-Cash processes, including sales order management, pricing, logistics execution integration, billing, returns, and related financial integration touchpoints.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently analyze, troubleshoot, and resolve complex SAP SD functional and configuration issues, including identifying root causes and implementing sustainable solutions.
  • Experience with incident management, change management, testing, and documentation practices. Experience with ServiceNow, SAP Solution Manager, or similar tools is an asset.
  • SAP SD or SAP S/4HANA certification, or another directly relevant SAP or supply chain certification, is considered an asset.
  • Demonstrated customer service skills and communication abilities, including the ability to explain SAP functionality and business process impacts to non-technical users.


Use of Artificial Intelligence in Recruitment

However, we advertise opportunities through third-party platforms such as Indeed, which may use AI-powered tools as part of their services. title: Logistics Planning Specialist - Europe
description:
Intelligently Moving Your World


XPENG is a leading technology company focused on designing, developing, manufacturing, and marketing intelligent mobility solutions, including electric vehicles (EVs), electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and robotics. We aim to create a thoughtful and empathetic future for mobility that enhances driving experience. Headquartered in Guangzhou, China, XPENG has regional offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Silicon Valley, and San Diego, and in 2021, we established our European headquarters in Amsterdam, along with offices in Copenhagen, Munich, Oslo, and Stockholm.

Our passionate and diverse team, with expertise in technology, finance, and the automotive industry, spans hubs in China, the US, and Europe. Together, we are forging our international presence as pioneers in the future of mobility.


Why should you be part of our success story?

XPENG Inc.'s American Depositary Shares (ADSs) have been listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) under the symbol 'XPEV' since August 27, 2020, and on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (SEHK) under the symbol '9868.HK' since July 7, 2021. In 2023, XPENG further strengthened its growth trajectory with a $724 million strategic investment from Volkswagen, solidifying its position in the global market. There has never been a more exciting time to join XPENG — a leader in smart electric vehicles and sustainable mobility solutions.


About the role

As a Logistics Planning Specialist, you will help plan how XPENG vehicles move from production plants and import ports to dealers across Europe. You will forecast vehicle volumes, translate them into transport and storage capacity plans, and work with internal teams and logistics providers to identify capacity constraints and improve the distribution network. You will report to the Logistics Planning Supervisor, Europe.


Key responsibilities

  • Develop short-, medium-, and long-term vehicle volume forecasts and translate them into transport and storage capacity plans.
  • Plan and optimize capacity across Ro-Ro and container shipping, rail, and road transport.
  • Monitor vehicle flows, inventory levels, and capacity utilization across ports, vehicle compounds, and the wider distribution network.
  • Align forecasts and capacity plans with Sales, Production, Order Management, Purchasing, and Operations.
  • Work with logistics providers and country teams to align available capacity with planned vehicle volumes and resolve capacity constraints.
  • Identify bottlenecks and capacity risks, and recommend ways to improve vehicle flows and reduce logistics costs.
  • Support distribution network design and expansion projects through long-term capacity planning, scenario analysis, and business cases.
  • Create KPI dashboards and planning reports to track vehicle flows, capacity utilization, and logistics performance.
  • Carry out other duties related to the role as assigned by the Logistics Planning Supervisor, in line with XPENG’s internal policies and procedures.


What you’ll bring

  • A degree in logistics, supply chain management, business, economics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 1–3 years of relevant experience in logistics or purchasing. Experience in automotive logistics, particularly finished vehicle logistics, is strongly preferred.
  • A good understanding of vehicle logistics and multimodal transportation.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to use data to identify capacity constraints and recommend practical solutions.
  • A structured, proactive approach and the ability to communicate clearly and collaborate with colleagues and external partners.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English. Additional languages, such as Mandarin or German, are a plus.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Excel and Access, and a willingness to learn other planning and reporting tools.


Next Steps:

To comply with GDPR, we can’t process your personal data without your given consent. Therefore, please apply directly via LinkedIn portal so that our team can proceed further.

For more information on how we process your personal data, please see: https://www.xpeng.com/policy

As part of our application process, certain positions at our company require a pre-employment screening to ensure the reliability and integrity of our employees. This screening is a standard procedure and may include components such as a Criminal Background Check from your current or previous country of residence over the past five years. Additionally, the process may involve an integrity questionnaire, verification of identification, diplomas, work experience, and consultation of the central insolvency register.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation in this important matter, as it helps us maintain the high standards expected by our team.


Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion:

At XPENG, we’re an equal-opportunity employer that values diversity and positively encourages applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of race, religion, sex, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability status or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

title: MRP Scheduler
description:
Flexi-Time, 33 Holidays, Frequent Work Events/Socials and State-Of-The-Art-Facilities are just a few of the benefits that the MRP Scheduler will enjoy whilst working with this award-winning engineering organisation.


Established over 100 years ago, this highly impressive engineering organisation is a vital partner to their high profile clientele. Operating out of a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility, they currently employ over 120 people and produce bespoke products for use in a variety of industries and types of facilities.


This employer is based in LEEDS, meaning that the successful MRP Scheduler will easily be able to commute from surrounding towns and cities including Bradford, Dewsbury, Huddersfield, Halifax, Wakefield, Castleford, Pontefract, Bingley and Keighley.


Key Responsibilities of the MRP Scheduler will include:

  • Run and manage MRP activities within the ERP system, reviewing planning outputs and converting requisitions and planned orders into firm purchase orders to support production requirements.
  • Monitor inventory levels and maintain accurate planning parameters including lead times, minimum order quantities, safety stock and supplier data to ensure material availability while controlling stockholding costs.
  • Analyse and action MRP exception messages, including expedite, de-expedite, reschedule and cancellation recommendations, to minimise supply chain disruption.
  • Place and manage purchase orders with suppliers, ensuring accuracy of pricing, quantities and delivery schedules, whilst securing timely order acknowledgements.
  • Proactively expedite critical materials, manage delivery risks and communicate material shortages to key stakeholders, implementing recovery plans to protect production schedules.
  • Resolve supplier delivery issues, invoice discrepancies and quantity variances, working closely with Production, Goods In, Quality and Finance teams to achieve effective resolutions.
  • Produce reports on material availability, supplier performance, open orders and inventory levels, whilst supporting cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement initiatives across planning and purchasing activities.


For the MRP Scheduler, we are keen to receive applications from individuals who possess:

  • 1-5 years' experience within Materials Planning, Production Planning, Supply Chain or Purchasing roles in a manufacturing environment, with a strong understanding of material flow and production support.
  • Proven experience using MRP/ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle or similar to manage demand planning, inventory and purchasing activities.

title: Internal IT Engineer
description:
Join Neysa as an Internal IT Engineer and become a pivotal part of creating a seamless, secure, and efficient digital workplace. At Neysa, we prioritize the role of technology in enhancing work productivity rather than causing hindrances. In this position, you will transcend traditional IT support by enhancing device security, ensuring optimal system performance, and facilitating a swift, trouble-free work experience for all employees.


As part of the Neysa team, you will engage in comprehensive IT engineering tasks that not only involve maintaining systems but also innovating processes to advance our digital infrastructure. Your contributions will be crucial in maintaining the balance between technology and user experience, ensuring that our digital environment operates smoothly and securely.


Skills & Qualification:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field
  • 7-15 years of hands-on experience in IT support or end-user computing environments
  • Strong expertise in macOS, Linux, and Windows administration, troubleshooting, and device configuration
  • Experience in endpoint security practices including patching, antivirus/EDR tools, device encryption, and access control
  • Solid understanding of networking fundamentals such as TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, VPNs, and firewalls
  • Proficiency with ticketing systems and structured incident management processes
  • Strong analytical and root-cause analysis skills to identify and resolve system issues effectively
  • Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration abilities to support team and user interactions
  • Familiarity with identity and access management concepts


Responsibilities:

  • Provide robust support for macOS, Windows, and other company devices ensuring seamless user experience
  • Set up and manage new devices for employees, covering installation of operating systems, applications, user accounts, and security tools
  • Troubleshoot complex issues related to operating systems, software conflicts, network, VPN, and collaboration tools to maintain workflow continuity
  • Maintain accurate records of all company IT devices, focusing on lifecycle management, warranty details, and compliance requirements
  • Coordinate with device vendors for warranty support, hardware checks, and replacements to ensure device reliability
  • Support and maintain office networks including Wi-Fi, LAN connections, and network cabling to facilitate connectivity
  • Manage conference room technology including video conferencing systems and LED screens to enhance meeting experiences
  • Monitor and maintain CCTV cameras and access control systems ensuring security and operational efficiency
  • Create and update IT documents, guides, and knowledge articles to empower users in resolving common issues independently
  • Test and assist in the deployment of new IT tools, device management systems, and productivity software to improve overall IT operations


Why This Role is a Unique Opportunity at Neysa:

This role offers the opportunity to work on complex, large-scale infrastructure systems that power AI-driven platforms. You will play a critical role in maintaining system reliability, handling high-impact incidents, and shaping operational excellence in a fast-growing AI ecosystem.


You'll gain deep exposure to enterprise infrastructure, automation practices, and next-generation AI workloads while contributing to a high-performance environment.


Team Culture and Inclusion:

  • Work in a collaborative, high-impact, and fast-paced environment
  • Be part of a culture that values ownership, innovation, and continuous learning
  • Thrive in an inclusive workplace where diverse ideas and perspectives are encouraged

title: Inventory & Logistics Analyst
description:
Position Summary: Inventory & Logistics Analyst

Company Overview

Established in 2007, ZEROCOR Tubulars (“ZEROCOR”) is a leading company that addresses erosion, corrosion, paraffin, and scale challenges in demanding oilfield environments. Headquartered in Calgary, AB, we offer extended-life tubulars and advanced protective coatings (including ENC) that significantly reduce maintenance and chemical costs. ZEROCOR is committed to providing reliable, cost-effective, and environmentally responsible solutions to the global energy sector.

Job Description

ZEROCOR is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Inventory & Logistics Analyst to enhance our supply chain and operational efficiency. Reporting directly to the General Manager, this role is essential for ensuring seamless coordination among marketing, sales support, and operations.

The successful candidate will manage the entire lifecycle of purchase orders, negotiate with vendors, and oversee raw material inventory across our network. You will serve as a key liaison, fostering strong relationships with vendors and customers to procure assets and ensure the successful completion of the sales process.


Key Duties & Responsibilities

Customer & Vendor Relations

  • Relationship Management: Build and maintain strategic partnerships with suppliers to leverage their technical capabilities and achieve business objectives.
  • Sales Support: Collaborate closely with the sales team to understand customer requirements and recommend appropriate technical product solutions.
  • Inquiry Resolution: Apply critical thinking to present solutions for supply chain disruptions and provide prompt, professional responses to internal and external inquiries about material availability, shortages, or logistics.
  • Market Growth Support: Identify opportunities to increase market share by optimizing delivery methods and enhancing service quality.

Procurement & Purchasing

  • Strategic Sourcing: Generate requests for quotes (RFQs) for pipe, pups, accessories, and freight; analyze quotes based on price, lead times, and historical vendor performance.
  • Procurement & Margin Analysis: Utilize pricing justification tools to calculate profit margins and document costs for accurate financial tracking.
  • Cost Optimization: Monitor supplier performance and lead cost-saving initiatives to enhance the bottom line.

Inventory & Logistics Management

  • Operations Coordination: Track incoming and outgoing shipments to ensure 100% inventory accuracy and on-time delivery.
  • Logistics Oversight: Manage the movement and assembly of pipes, ensuring all ERP system entries (including purchases, transfers, and changes) are completed accurately.
  • Problem Solving: Resolve discrepancies in inventory assets during the pre-sale, post-sale, and release stages to ensure seamless project execution.


Reporting & Auditing

  • Data Analysis: Generate monthly management reports, including sales data and inventory reconciliation.
  • Auditing: Lead routine inventory audits and reconcile physical yard records with digital system levels.

Product & Technical Expertise

  • Inventory Mastery: Maintain comprehensive knowledge of current inventory, including size, grade, weight, length, and thread connections.
  • Process Familiarity: Understand the differences between international and domestic products, as well as the capabilities of third-party processors and vendors.
  • Technical Support: Deliver clear technical information to the sales team regarding value-added environmental solutions and relevant product recommendations.


Education & Experience

  • Education: A secondary education is required. Post-secondary training in Supply Chain, Logistics, or Business is strongly preferred.
  • Experience: A minimum of 2 years of experience in customer service, sales operations support, purchasing, or inventory management is considered an asset.
  • Systems: Proficient skills in Microsoft 365 and SharePoint are necessary. Experience with Cin7Core (Inventory Management) and XERO (Accounting) is a significant advantage.
  • Technical Aptitude: Ability to learn and manage complex inventory standards, including order dimensions, metric tons, and chemistry limitations.

Skills & Qualifications

  • Precision: Excellent attention to detail and strong organizational skills.
  • Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication abilities, along with a positive “can-do” attitude.
  • Adaptability: Ability to excel in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with changing priorities.
  • Judgment: Utilizes sound logic to resolve inventory issues and monitor supplier performance.
  • Logistics: Must possess a valid Driver’s license and be willing to be on call, with occasional travel to local yards, approximately 5-10%.


Compensation & Benefits

ZEROCOR offers a competitive, performance-based compensation package that includes:

  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision benefits.
  • Flexible paid vacation.
  • Up to 5% matching contributions for a Deferred Profit-Sharing Plan (DPSP).
  • Access to an on-site fitness center.
  • Competitive salary, quarterly team bonus, and additional information will be discussed during the interview.

Location: Calgary, AB (100% in-office, downtown). Travel may be required as needed.

Contact: To apply for this opportunity, please submit your resume and cover letter to info@zerocor.com.

  • We appreciate all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Materials Management
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

A utilities client in the Houston area is looking for a Materials Management Specialist to join their team. This team supports the electric organization at the client and is responsible for all materials management for high voltage equipment. The Materials Management Specialist is responsible for the development, implementation, and management of companywide supply chain inventory strategies for assigned commodities, consistent with Corporate and Departmental policies and procedures. They lead all aspects of planning, monitoring and delivery of inventory material utilized in the Supply Chain; monitor material usage, future requirements, and key supplier relationships in conjunction with Procurement; is aware of market and industry trends/conditions, market pricing, quality and delivery requirements, and other factors in the performance of duties. The Materials Management Specialist is required to interface with Vendors (sales/project management personnel), internal clients (users), auditors, Procurement, etc. to achieve total overall value to the Company; thus, must be able to communicate effectively and efficiently.


Summary:

  • Project Readiness: Serve as the Materials Management owner for project readiness across assigned construction and capital projects, ensuring critical materials and equipment are visible, assigned, tracked, and aligned to project execution milestones.
  • Delivery Monitoring: Monitor long-lead and critical-path equipment from order visibility through manufacturing, factory testing, shipment, delivery, staging, and project handoff.
  • Stakeholder Coordination: Partner with Construction, Engineering, Procurement, EPC contractors, Owner's Engineers, OEM suppliers, Operations, and project leadership to identify risks early and drive clear mitigation plans.
  • Risk Management: Translate material constraints, supplier delays, manufacturing issues, logistics risks, and quality holds into concise project impact statements, action plans, and escalation recommendations.
  • Executive Visibility: Provide leadership-ready reporting on project material readiness, critical equipment status, supplier performance, open actions, risk ratings, and recovery plans.


Job Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the single point of accountability within Materials Management for material readiness across assigned capital projects and critical equipment categories.

  • Monitor delivery status for long-lead and critical-path equipment including transformers, breakers, switchgear, structures, conductor, cable, controls, and other strategic materials.

Skills:

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

NICE TO HAVE SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

title: Supplier Performance Lead [T500-29669]
description:
About Officeworks:

Officeworks’ purpose is “we bring big ideas to life at low prices”. It’s how we create shared value for customers, team members, suppliers, communities and shareholders.

We are Australia’s leading omnichannel retailer of complete technology solutions, stationery, furniture, art supplies, and learning resources. We also offer services including Print & Create, and Geeks2U.

Our products and services provide solutions to our diverse range of customers across Australia from households, students, small to large sized businesses, governments and schools.

Our culture is built on beginning with customer, doing the right thing, executing with accountability, and leading with ambition. We are one team who are proud to “wear the blues” and deliver for our customers.

We are an inclusive, forward-thinking organisation where diverse perspectives enable innovation, continuous improvement and better outcomes for our customers and teams. The work we do plays an important role in helping Australians work, l:earn, create and connect.


Individual Contributor:

  • Lives our Officeworks values and behaviours
  • Proactively contributes to a safe working environment, escalates appropriately if there are unsafe conditions or inappropriate behaviour
  • Operates in line with applicable Officeworks company policies and Code of Conduct
  • Demonstrates a strong sense of personal accountability and curiosity to learn and develop
  • Contributes to an inclusive and respectful environment where diverse perspectives are valued and everyone feels safe to speak up and belong


Our Values:

Our values shape the way we work, our behaviours and how we interact with each other, our customers, suppliers and communities.


We begin with customer:

  • We start with our customer’ needs in every decision.
  • We offer simple, helpful and affordable solutions.
  • We listen, learn and continuously improve.


We do the right thing:

  • We lead with integrity and care for our team communities and planet.
  • We work together safely and treat everyone with respect, inclusion, and trust.
  • We collaborate across teams and think Officeworks-wide.


We execute with accountability:

  • We are accountable for our decisions, actions, results, and mistakes.
  • We stay across the details and focus on delivering what matters.
  • We move with pace and agility to deliver outcomes.


We lead with ambition:

  • We set bold ambitions that help us to win and transform.
  • We are courageous with new ideas.
  • We focus on transformation, not incremental steps.


The Commercial team sits at the heart of Officeworks’ growth agenda. This function brings together customer needs, product innovation, services, supplier partnerships, merchandise planning, and channel growth to shape what Officeworks sells, how it competes, and the value it delivers across Retail, B2B, Government, and Education. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to one of the business’s most commercially impactful areas.

The team plays a key role in evolving Officeworks’ product and service offering, accelerating growth in high-potential channels (such as B2B and Education), expanding private label and exclusive ranges, strengthening supplier partnerships, and unlocking emerging category opportunities across areas like technology, gaming, mobility, VR, print, installation, telco, and managed services. You will help build commercial capability from the ground up, shaping scalable ways of working, strengthening planning and decision-making, and driving outcomes that impact sales, margin, customer experience, inventory performance, and long-term growth.


These roles are best suited for people who enjoy:

  • thriving in a growth-focused retail environment where commercial decisions directly influence customers, sales, margin, and competitiveness
  • contributing to key growth areas, including B2B, Education, Government, private label, exclusive products, and emerging categories
  • using insights (customer, competitor, category, supplier, financial, inventory) to identify opportunities and inform decisions
  • collaborating cross-functionally to turn commercial strategy into practical outcomes


Why this role exists:

This role is responsible for improving supplier cost and trading-term outcomes by providing the frameworks, analytics and tools required for better commercial decisions. The role identifies opportunities to drive margin dollars, recover value and respond consistently to supplier cost-price increases across commercial portfolios.

The role builds scalable negotiation playbooks, automated workflows and exception reporting that strengthen commercial discipline and reduce reliance on manual analysis. It enables Category teams to approach supplier reviews with stronger evidence, consistent methods and clear commercial guardrails, without directly owning supplier negotiations.


Trading Terms and Commercial Governance:

  • Develop, implement and maintain enterprise trading-term frameworks across commercial category portfolios.
  • Analyse supplier economics, rebates, funding arrangements and category margin drivers to identify commercial improvement opportunities.
  • Develop benchmarks, decision guardrails and trade-off models to support consistent evaluation of supplier terms.
  • Monitor adherence to approved trading terms, identifying material deviations, uncollected value and commercial risks.
  • Maintain clear records of trading-term opportunities, decisions and outcomes to support governance and value reporting.


Cost-Price Increase Analysis and Mitigation:

  • Build and maintain automated workflows for receiving, assessing and tracking supplier cost-price increase requests.
  • Evaluate supplier submissions using commodity indices, market benchmarks, cost-component models and historical cost movements.
  • Quantify the financial impact of proposed cost changes, including margin exposure and unrecovered cost.
  • Develop evidence-based mitigation scenarios, including delays, phased increases, challenges and alternative commercial offsets.
  • Track cost-price increase outcomes across portfolios, measuring margin value preserved or recovered through intervention.
  • Maintain accurate workflow records, approval evidence and exception reporting for cost-price increase decisions.


Negotiation Tools and Category Enablement:

  • Develop category negotiation playbooks that combine supplier insights, cost benchmarks, trading-term opportunities and recommended negotiation positions.
  • Build commercial models, supplier profiles and should-cost analysis to strengthen preparation for supplier reviews.
  • Translate complex commercial analysis into clear negotiation options, trade-offs and decision points.
  • Guide the application of consistent, evidence-based negotiation methods across Category teams.
  • Review negotiation outcomes and feedback to improve playbooks, benchmarks and analytical tools.
  • Monitor adoption and use of Better Buying tools across priority categories.


Exception Reporting and Commercial Analytics:

  • Design exception-reporting frameworks and materiality thresholds that identify margin leakage, missing rebates and uncollected trading-term value.
  • Extract, normalise and analyse commercial data across SAP, STIBO/PIM, Snowflake and supporting data sources.
  • Develop dashboards and reporting in Power BI or Tableau to track trading-term value, cost-price mitigation and category adoption.
  • Investigate financial and commercial variances, identifying root causes and recommended corrective actions.
  • Validate reported benefits and maintain clear definitions for identified, approved and delivered commercial value.
  • Produce concise insights that highlight priority risks, opportunities and required decisions.


Technical Guidance and Continuous Improvement:

  • Provide technical guidance to analysts on Better Buying methods, commercial modelling and data-quality requirements.
  • Document analytical methods, playbook structures, workflow controls and standard operating procedures.
  • Define business requirements for systems, data and automation enhancements.
  • Support solution testing and implementation, ensuring changes meet commercial, data and control requirements.
  • Identify opportunities to automate recurring analysis, reporting and workflow activity.
  • Maintain current knowledge of supplier economics, trading-term practices and cost drivers relevant to retail categories.


Who you will be working with:

  • Category Leadership: Partner with Category Managers, Category Planners, and Category Assistants to provide negotiation playbooks, cost-stack insights, and trading terms guidance.
  • Commercial Leadership & Finance: Collaborate with the Pricing and Better Buying Manager, Commercial Leadership Team, and Finance business partners to report on margin recovery and trading terms performance.
  • Technology & Data Partners: Work closely with Technology & Data, Product Data, and Legal, Risk & Compliance teams to govern automated systems, data feeds, and contract controls.
  • External Market Providers: Liaise with market data benchmarking vendors, analytics technology partners, and external advisers to incorporate external market intelligence into playbooks


What success looks like:

  • Trading Terms Value: Quantifiable commercial value identified and delivered through trading terms optimization and contract reviews.
  • Cost Increase Mitigation: High percentage of supplier cost-price increases mitigated, delayed, or offset through structured playbooks.
  • Playbook Adoption: High percentage of priority commercial categories utilizing current automated negotiation playbooks during trade reviews.
  • Exception Reporting Precision: Accurate exception reporting delivered within SLAs, with a high proportion of material exceptions actioned by category teams.
  • Demonstrates behaviours aligned to Officeworks’ values, contributing to a respectful, inclusive and high-performing culture


Qualifications and work experience:

Essential:

  • Education: Tertiary qualification in Commerce, Business, Finance, Economics, Analytics, or a related discipline is required (or equivalent senior better-buying, procurement analytics, or commercial experience).
  • Experience: 5–7+ years in commercial analytics, procurement analytics, category management, or a related commercial function
  • Commercial Frameworks: Advanced knowledge of trading terms, cost-price management, supplier economics, and retail margin drivers
  • Technical Analytics Mastery: Strong commercial modelling, financial analytics, and data-visualization capability (Power BI / Tableau) using large data sets
  • Process & Tool Engineering: Practical experience building category negotiation playbooks, automated CPI workflow systems, and governance controls
  • Risk & Exception Management: Sound understanding of exception-reporting design, variance threshold configuration, and commercial risk escalation
  • Analyst Guidance: Demonstrated capability to guide, review, and mentor analysts across analytical tasks and commercial priorities


Preferred:

  • Experience working with enterprise SAP pricing architecture, STIBO/PIM, Snowflake, or automated workflow platforms
  • Direct exposure to FMCG or retail procurement analytics, cost-breakdown modelling, or supplier trade negotiation support
  • Practical experience within high-SKU omnichannel retailor FMCG environments

title: IT Infrastructure Manager
description:
We are looking for an experienced and technically strong IT Manager to manage key customer IT infrastructure, oversee managed services operations, and lead a team of approximately 10 technical professionals.


The IT Manager will be responsible for end-to-end infrastructure management of the company's top five assigned customers, ensuring smooth IT operations, timely issue resolution, effective team coordination, customer satisfaction, and compliance with agreed service levels.


The candidate should have hands-on experience in IT infrastructure, networking, servers, virtualization, storage, backup, security, and customer-facing technical service delivery.


The role requires strong technical troubleshooting abilities, leadership skills, ownership of customer issues, and the ability to manage multiple customer environments independently.


Key Roles & Responsibilities:

  • Take complete responsibility for IT infrastructure management of the top five assigned customers.
  • Understand each customer's IT environment, infrastructure architecture, business applications, and operational requirements.
  • Act as the primary technical point of contact for assigned customers.
  • Proactively identify infrastructure risks, performance issues, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Ensure timely troubleshooting and resolution of customer infrastructure issues.
  • Coordinate with internal technical teams, OEMs, and external vendors whenever required.
  • Conduct scheduled customer interactions to review ongoing issues, infrastructure health, and service performance.
  • Maintain updated customer infrastructure documentation, including network diagrams, asset inventories, configurations, and escalation matrices.
  • Ensure customer satisfaction through regular communication, proactive support, and timely issue resolution.
  • Manage day-to-day IT infrastructure operations, including servers, storage, virtualization, networking, backup, and security systems.
  • Oversee Windows/Linux servers, Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, and related infrastructure services.
  • Manage and support LAN, WAN, VLAN, routing, switching, firewalls, VPNs, and wireless networking environments.
  • Ensure the availability, performance, and reliability of customer infrastructure.
  • Coordinate infrastructure maintenance, upgrades, patching, configuration changes, and preventive maintenance activities.
  • Ensure regular backup monitoring, restoration testing, and disaster recovery readiness.
  • Review infrastructure alerts, system performance, and recurring technical issues.
  • Provide technical guidance and support during critical infrastructure incidents.
  • Ensure infrastructure changes follow approved change management procedures.
  • Take ownership of managed services delivery for assigned customers.
  • Ensure services are delivered according to agreed contracts, SLAs, and customer expectations.
  • Monitor daily service operations and review open incidents, service requests, and pending activities.
  • Ensure timely ticket assignment, acknowledgment, escalation, resolution, and closure.
  • Monitor service delivery performance and identify areas requiring improvement.
  • Ensure preventive maintenance activities are completed as scheduled.
  • Conduct periodic service review meetings with customers.
  • Prepare monthly service reports covering ticket performance, infrastructure availability, recurring incidents, and improvement actions.
  • Ensure effective coordination between remote support, onsite engineers, and internal infrastructure teams.
  • Identify service delivery gaps and implement corrective actions.
  • Take complete responsibility for ticketing portal operations and ticket assignment management.
  • Supervise the Event Monitoring and IT Operations teams.
  • Ensure infrastructure monitoring alerts are reviewed, categorized, prioritized, and assigned appropriately.
  • Track critical incidents and ensure timely escalation to the relevant technical teams.
  • Ensure all customer issues are properly recorded and updated in the ticketing system.
  • Monitor ticket aging, SLA breaches, repeated incidents, and unresolved customer issues.
  • Ensure proper incident documentation, root cause analysis (RCA), and closure confirmation.
  • Review daily ticket dashboards and pending escalations.
  • Improve ticket handling processes to reduce resolution time and prevent recurring incidents.
  • Ensure monitoring events are converted into actionable incidents whenever required.
  • Lead and manage an IT Operations team of approximately 10 engineers, including infrastructure, networking, and support personnel.
  • Assign daily responsibilities based on technical skills, workload, and customer priorities.
  • Monitor individual engineer performance, productivity, and task completion.
  • Conduct daily operational reviews and weekly technical team meetings.
  • Ensure team members follow company processes, ticketing procedures, escalation matrices, and reporting requirements.
  • Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and troubleshooting support.
  • Identify technical skill gaps and arrange training and knowledge-sharing sessions.
  • Ensure adequate engineer availability and backup resource planning.
  • Review Daily Activity Reports (DAR), ticket updates, and pending tasks.
  • Conduct periodic performance reviews and provide constructive feedback.
  • Ensure accountability, discipline, teamwork, and timely completion of assigned responsibilities.
  • Maintain professional and regular communication with assigned customers.
  • Schedule periodic meetings to understand customer concerns, technical issues, and upcoming requirements.
  • Coordinate between customers, internal engineers, project teams, sales teams, and OEM partners.
  • Provide regular updates on ongoing incidents, project activities, and service improvements.
  • Handle technical escalations and ensure appropriate resolution within agreed timelines.
  • Participate in customer meetings for infrastructure planning, upgrades, and new requirements.
  • Build strong customer relationships through responsiveness, transparency, and service quality.
  • Ensure Minutes of Meetings (MOM), action items, responsibilities, and timelines are documented and tracked.
  • Actively participate in identifying and understanding new infrastructure requirements from assigned customers.
  • Conduct initial technical discussions and requirement-gathering meetings.
  • Coordinate with the Sales and Presales teams for technical feasibility, solution discussions, and proposals.
  • Provide infrastructure assessments and technical recommendations.
  • Participate in project planning, implementation coordination, and technical reviews.
  • Ensure smooth handover of completed projects to the IT Operations or Managed Services teams.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline.

title: Inventory Coordinator
description:
Inventory Coordinator

Manufacturing sector

Monday to Thursday 8am-4.30pm & Friday 8am-3.30pm (39hr week)

£42,000 - £48,000 per annum

Red Hill, Worcester


Purpose

We are excited to be recruiting for a brand-new position for our Worcester based client who specialise in critical component manufacturing (low volume, high value precision made pieces – this is a place where you will take great pride in what you manufacture). Our client is in need of an Inventory Coordinator who will be responsible for maintaining accurate stores/inventory records, ensuring stock availability for production, coordinating material movements, and supporting procurement and warehouse activities. The role plays a critical part in ensuring uninterrupted manufacturing operations through effective inventory control, stock accuracy, and timely replenishment of materials.


Essential background needed

  • Previous experience in inventory control, stock management, warehouse operations, or supply chain coordination within an ISO 9001 manufacturing environment.
  • Experience using ERP/MRP systems (Oracle would be advantageous)
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills (Excel, Access, Teams + SharePoint)
  • Good understanding of inventory management principles.
  • Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Strong organisational and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work effectively across production, purchasing, and warehouse teams.

Key Responsibilities

Data & Reporting

  • Produce inventory reports, stock valuation reports, and KPI metrics.
  • Analyse inventory trends and recommend improvements.
  • Update material master data and inventory records.
  • Assist with audits and compliance requirements.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve inventory processes and reduce waste.
  • Support lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Assist in the implementation of inventory management best practices.

Inventory Control

  • Monitor and maintain accurate inventory records within the ERP/MRP system.
  • Perform regular cycle counts and support full stock takes.
  • Investigate and resolve inventory discrepancies and variances.
  • Ensure all stock movements are accurately recorded and processed.
  • Maintain inventory accuracy targets and KPI reporting.

Production Support

  • Work closely with Production Planners to support manufacturing requirements.

Purchasing & Replenishment

  • Raise purchase requisitions and purchase orders for approved materials.
  • Monitor supplier deliveries and follow up on overdue orders.
  • Maintain agreed minimum and maximum stock levels.
  • Support supplier performance monitoring and inventory optimisation initiatives.

Warehouse & Logistics Coordination

  • Coordinate goods receipt, inspection, storage, and dispatch activities.
  • Ensure inventory is stored safely and organised efficiently.
  • Work with warehouse personnel to maintain stock location accuracy.
  • Support inbound and outbound logistics planning as required.

title: CATALOGING & INVENTORY EXECUTIVE (MANUFACTURING MUST)
description:

title: Supplier Relations Executive (Hotels, Crew and Accommodation)
description:
About the Role


Our Supplier Relations Executive is responsible for supporting the development, management and performance of CMAC's accommodation and travel supplier network, ensuring hotel, accommodation and other travel partners deliver reliable, compliant and commercially effective services that support operational and customer requirements.


You will work closely with hotel providers, accommodation partners, airline customers and internal stakeholders to support supplier onboarding, relationship management, performance monitoring and commercial activities. The role plays a key part in maintaining a resilient accommodation network capable of supporting airline crew, passenger disruption (IROPs), corporate travel and operational requirements.


You will help identify and onboard new accommodation partners, maintain supplier records and performance data, support commercial negotiations and contribute to ensuring CMAC has the right supplier coverage in the right locations to meet customer demand.


The role combines supplier management, hospitality relationship management and commercial support, making it ideal for someone with experience in hotels, accommodation, hospitality, travel or supplier management who enjoys building partnerships and contributing to operational excellence.


What Success Looks Like

  • Supplier relationships are maintained professionally and proactively.
  • Supplier records, contracts and performance data remain accurate and up to date.
  • Supplier performance supports operational and customer requirements.
  • New suppliers are onboarded efficiently and effectively.
  • Customer complaints, supplier issues and invoice queries are resolved promptly.
  • Supplier coverage, quality and availability support business objectives.
  • Reporting and supplier management information provide meaningful insight.
  • Departmental KPIs, SLAs and service standards are consistently achieved.
  • Continuous improvement opportunities are identified and implemented.


Core Responsibilities


Supplier Relationship Support

  • Build and maintain positive working relationships with suppliers and operational partners.
  • Support Supplier Relations Managers in managing supplier portfolios and engagement activities.
  • Act as a day-to-day contact for supplier enquiries and communications.
  • Promote collaborative and professional relationships across the supplier network.
  • Support supplier meetings, reviews and engagement activities.
  • Represent CMAC professionally in all supplier interactions.


Supplier Performance & Network Development

  • Support monitoring of supplier performance against agreed KPIs and service standards.
  • Assist with supplier reviews, audits and performance assessments.
  • Identify emerging supplier issues and escalate where appropriate.
  • Support supplier recruitment and onboarding activities.
  • Help maintain a resilient supplier network capable of meeting operational demand.
  • Contribute to supplier improvement initiatives and best practice activities.


Commercial & Operational Support

  • Assist with supplier negotiations, tenders and commercial activities.
  • Analyse supplier activity, utilisation and commercial performance.
  • Support initiatives that improve supplier value, margin and operational efficiency.
  • Assist operational teams in resolving supplier-related service issues.
  • Support customer and supplier requirements through effective coordination.
  • Contribute to business growth by supporting supplier capability and availability.


Supplier Administration & Governance

  • Maintain supplier databases, documentation and operational records.
  • Ensure supplier information remains accurate, complete and up to date.
  • Support supplier compliance activities, audits and governance requirements.
  • Maintain records relating to supplier performance, contracts and service standards.
  • Assist with the preparation of reports, reviews and supplier communications.
  • Ensure governance activities are completed in line with company standards.


Stakeholder Collaboration & Customer Service

  • Work closely with Operations, Planning, Commercial and Finance teams.
  • Support the resolution of customer complaints, supplier disputes and invoice queries.
  • Coordinate information between suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • Ensure supplier service expectations align with customer requirements.
  • Support the delivery of excellent customer and supplier experiences.
  • Promote effective communication and collaboration across business functions.


Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Produce supplier reports, performance information and administrative updates.
  • Monitor supplier trends and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Support analysis of supplier performance and operational data.
  • Contribute to process improvement and efficiency initiatives.
  • Maintain awareness of market conditions, supplier developments and industry changes.
  • Support a culture of continuous improvement, accountability and operational excellence.


About You


You are an organised and relationship-focused professional who enjoys working with suppliers, analysing information and supporting business performance. You take pride in delivering excellent service and building strong working relationships with both internal and external stakeholders.


You are proactive, commercially aware and comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. You enjoy solving problems, maintaining high standards and contributing to the success of the wider team.


You thrive in environments where collaboration, attention to detail and customer focus are critical to success.


Your Expertise

  • Experience in Supplier Management, Hotel Contracting, Accommodation Procurement, Hospitality Sales, Travel Procurement, Account Management or a similar supplier-focused role.
  • Experience working with hotels, accommodation providers, hospitality groups or travel suppliers.
  • Understanding of accommodation sourcing, supplier onboarding and supplier relationship management.
  • Strong relationship building and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent organisational and administrative capability.
  • Experience maintaining supplier records, contracts and performance information.
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to interpret performance data and identify trends.
  • Excellent communication and customer service skills.
  • Experience supporting supplier onboarding, performance reviews and commercial activities.
  • Ability to work independently whilst contributing as part of a wider team.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
  • Experience within hospitality, travel management, aviation, airline crew accommodation, mobility or service-led industries would be highly advantageous.
  • Understanding of airline crew accommodation, passenger disruption (IROP) environments or operational travel services would be beneficial.
  • Strong commercial awareness and problem-solving capability.


About Us


CMAC Group is a fast‑growing leader in global passenger transport and accommodation solutions - trusted by airlines, rail operators, major corporations and emergency breakdown providers to keep people moving safely and seamlessly, 24/7/365.


Since 2007, we’ve built a powerful technology-led aggregation platform that connects clients to a vast, reliable global supply network, enabling us to move over 5 million passengers every year across the UK, Europe and beyond.


Our portfolio of specialist brands include Suntransfers.com, CoachHireComparison.co.uk, Minicabit.com and CheckedSafe, which gives us unmatched capability to coordinate transport and accommodation at scale, even in the most complex or time critical situations.


Backed by ComfortDelGro, one of the world’s leading mobility groups, CMAC continues to operate with the agility and innovation of an independent business whilst benefiting from the strength, stability and global reach of a major international parent company.


At CMAC, you’ll join a team that thrives on solving real world challenges, shaping the future of mobility and delivering exceptional service when it matters most. If you’re driven, curious and excited by meaningful impact, you’ll feel right at home here.


CMAC Group actively promotes equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI).


EDI is extremely important to us and we work hard to ensure that everyone connected with CMAC - whether employees, customers, Board Members, suppliers, or partners - has genuine and equal opportunities to participate in our organisation.


We welcome and support people of all backgrounds and identities, regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.


Our aim is to create an environment where everyone’s rights, dignity, and individuality are respected.


We value the unique contribution each person brings to our team and business, and we are committed to building an environment where everyone feels included and able to thrive.


CMAC Group is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates and are committed to ensuring fair, accessible, and equitable treatment for all applicants and employees.
